(the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), reported net income for the third quarter of 2026 of $16.8 million, or $0.50 per diluted common share, compared to net income of $18.9 million, or $0.56 per diluted common share, for the second quarter of 2026, and net income of $14.3 million, or $0.43 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Third Quarter 2026 Highlights</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Pre-tax Pre-provision Income (&#8220;PTPP&#8221;)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">,</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">a non-U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">(1)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> financial measure &#8211; PTPP for the third quarter of 2026 increased $1.5 million to $27.5 million, from $26.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. PTPP increased primarily due to an increase in interest income of $2.6 million and a decrease in noninterest expense of $405 thousand. The increase in net interest income was partially offset by a decrease in noninterest income of $1.2 million and an increase in interest expense of $390 thousand. PTPP for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $76.4 million compared to $63.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Return on Average Assets (&#8220;ROAA&#8221;)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> &#8211; The Company reported ROAA of 1.08% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.24% for the second quarter of 2026 and 0.95% for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted ROAA &#8211; non-GAAP</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">(1) </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">was 1.16% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 1.34% for the second quarter of 2026 and 1.05% for the third quarter of 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Net Interest Margin (&#8220;NIM&#8221;) </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211; Net interest income for the third quarter of 2026 increased $2.2 million to $55.1 million compared to the second quarter of 2026. NIM increased 8 basis points (&#8220;bps&#8221;) to 3.78% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026. NIM excluding accretion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">(1)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> increased for the comparable periods from 3.45% to 3.50%. Excluding accretion interest, loan yields increased 4 bp and funding costs decreased 2 bps for the comparable periods. Net interest income increased due to elevated accretion income from loan payoffs, partially offset by a slightly higher interest expense driven by municipal deposits.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Capital Management &#8211; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Book value per share increased to $18.59 at September&#160;30, 2026 from $18.44 at June&#160;30, 2026 and $17.27 at September&#160;30, 2025. During the quarter ended September&#160;30, 2026, </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">the Company declared a dividend of $0.14 per share and </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">repurchased 148,006 shares of its outstanding common stock for approximately $3.4 million.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Asset Quality </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211; Nonperforming assets were </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1.27%</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> of total assets at September&#160;30, 2026, an increase from </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1.09%</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> at June&#160;30, 2026 and an </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">increase</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> from </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">0.45%</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> at September&#160;30, 2025. Classified assets were </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1.61%</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> of total assets at September&#160;30, 2026, an </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">increase</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> when compared to </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1.41%</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> at June&#160;30, 2026 and </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">0.83%</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> at September&#160;30, 2025. The allowance for credit losses (&#8220;ACL&#8221;) was $59.6 million at both September&#160;30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, and $58.7 million at June&#160;30, 2026. The ACL as a percentage of loans increased to 1.21% at September&#160;30, 2026 compared to 1.20% at June&#160;30, 2026 and decreased compared to </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1.22% </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">at September&#160;30, 2025.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.5pt">Operating Leverage </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8211;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The efficiency ratio for the third quarter of 2026 was 56.15%, compared to 57.76% in the second quarter of 2026 and 61.00% for the third quarter of 2025. The adjusted efficiency ratio &#8211; non-GAAP</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">(1)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">, which excludes amortization of intangibles, was 53.30% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 54.49% for the second quarter of 2026 and 57.30% for the third quarter of 2025. Management anticipates ongoing expense management of professional services and technology investments will result in continued improvements in operating leverage over time. </font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">&#8220;Our third quarter reflected very strong core earnings, driven by continued expansion in net interest margin, growth in net interest income and lower noninterest expense, which further improved operating leverage,&#8221; stated James (&#8220;Jimmy&#8221;) M. Burke, President and Chief Executive Officer of Shore Bancshares, Inc. &#8220;Pre-tax, pre-provision income increased 5.6% from the prior quarter, reflecting our disciplined approach to balance sheet management, the strength of our deposit franchise and our focus on operational execution.</font></div><div style="border-bottom:1pt solid #000000;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:10pt;opacity:1;width:150pt"></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">(1)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> See the Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Measures tables.</font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:27pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:right"><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Net income for the quarter was impacted by a higher provision for credit losses, primarily related to a partial charge-off on a multifamily relationship that we downgraded last year. As we pursued an exit from these credits, updated valuations reflected property-specific issues that reduced collateral values. Our approach is to address potential credit problems as early as possible, and our core performance gives us the flexibility to do so. Capital levels remained strong, book value per share increased and we continued to return capital to shareholders through our quarterly dividend and share repurchases. Going forward, we remain focused on prudent growth, continually managing expenses and creating long-term value for our shareholders.&#8221;</font></div><div id="i3e000039bfb04c6f8d3aca4c7c730bde_7"></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Balance Sheet Review</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Total assets were $6.45 billion at September&#160;30, 2026, an increase of $302.9 million from June&#160;30, 2026. The increase was primarily due to an increase in cash and cash equivalents of $197.4 million, an increase in available for sale securities of $93.5 million and an increase in loans of $24.9 million. Total assets increased $195.5 million, or 3.1%, when compared to $6.26 billion at December&#160;31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in cash and cash equivalents of $99.5 million and an increase in our investment securities portfolio of $101.7 million. The increases in cash and cash equivalents during the quarter and year were primarily driven by the seasonality of municipal deposits. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">CRE loans (excluding land and construction) were $2.58&#160;billion at September&#160;30, 2026 compared to $2.64&#160;billion at December&#160;31, 2025.
